newsitem.title: UK: Phibro cuts IPE operation, stays in cash oil marke.
newsitem.headline: Phibro cuts IPE operation, stays in cash oil marke.

text.p: Salomon Inc's energy trading subsidiary Phibro has scaled down oil trading activities in Europe but will maintain a strong presence in cash markets, trading sources said on Thursday.

Phibro, one of the biggest players on international energy markets over the past decade, had halved its futures trading team at London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) to six from 12 staff in the past week, the traders said.
Around a dozen middle and back office support staff had also left the company in recent weeks, dealers said.
Traders said that, in addition, two specialist physical crude oil traders working Russian and Mediterranean markets, had left the company without being replaced.
But they said that, contrary to rumours, Phibro was not pulling out of physical oil trading in Europe and any staff reductions reflected new minimum financial thresholds for trading performance.
Phibro continued to trade North Sea physical and paper (cash) crude markets with four traders plus European cash fuel oil and gas oil.
Salomon recently removed a thorn from its side with the sale of its oil refining and marketing unit, Basis Petroleum Inc.
Prior to that, Salomon had split Phibro from Basis Petroleum.
Phibro has performed erratically in recent years due to volatile oil prices and oil refining losses it carried before the Basis spin-off.
Salomon reported net revenues for Phibro at $25 million for the first quarter of 1997 down from $235 million in the same period a year earlier.
Last October Phibro pulled out of trading coal, coke and fertilisers. --Sam Arnold-Forster, London newsroom +44 171 542 4984
